title_original: Peter Nagy, Adventurous Artist Turned Sharp-Sighted Dealer, Dies at 67
editorial_title_zh: 富有冒险精神的艺术家、后来成为目光敏锐艺廊经营者的Peter Nagy去世，享年67岁
editorial_excerpt_zh: 他经营的Nature Morte画廊帮助印度在全球化艺术界确立了重要地位。

article_text:
Peter Nagy , an artist who became a star of the East Village in 1980s New York before ascending as one of India’s leading art dealers in the 1990s, has died at 67. Nature Morte , the New Delhi–based gallery that he ran, said that he had battled a long illness in a statement posted to social media.

“He lived exactly as he chose: fearlessly, irreverently and wildly free,” the gallery wrote . “He had no patience for convention for its own sake, and endless patience for ideas, for artists and for the people he loved. He made the art world more daring, more generous and far more interesting.”

The arc of Nagy’s career was an unusual one. He fostered a generation of appropriation-minded artists based in New York and helped stake a claim for India’s importance to the international art world. And in his art, he found his own take on commodification and reproducibility, two notions frequently addressed by artists of his generation.

In his own practice, Nagy pondered heady subject matter related to the corporatization of art and transmission of ideas and images across the globe. His works of the 1980s borrowed corporate logos and pictures from art history textbooks, showing that everything and anything could be endlessly copied until it signified nothing much at all. These early pieces synced with the bitter mindset of the Pictures Generation of the late 1970s and early ’80s, whose artists took up appropriation as a means of testing authorship and ownership.

“People don’t have anything to express, except the trademark,” Nagy said in one interview from the early ’80s. “We’re being fed information all the time.”

Relying on his education in design, Nagy would often clip out images and collage them together, using a similar method enlisted to create paste-ups used in the creation of print media in the pre-Photoshop age. He excised elements of floor plans, art books, and advertisements, then mashed together. Often, he would then Xerox the collages, blowing them up in the process.

The works looked machine-made, even when they were not. “The irony is that they’re handmade paintings that look like they might be computer-derived,” he told ARTnews in 2020 amid a revival of interest in his art. “I was interested in the degradation of the image and the information the image contained. I also thought there was additional information to be gleaned from that degradation. I was really into this idea: making copies of copies and noticing how long the original information maintained its integrity the longer I continued.”

Nagy went on to exhibit his spare art during the mid-’80s with International with Monument Gallery, a New York space that brought early attention to Jeff Koons, Ashley Bickerton, and Peter Halley. Later, he showed with dealers Jay Gorney and Nicole Klagsbrun.

At the same time, Nagy was running Nature Morte, which he founded with Alan Belcher in the East Village in 1982. He initially ran the gallery out of an East 10th Street storefront that he and Belcher rented for $500 a month. “We had no fucking clue what we were doing, but it was small and it was easy,” Nagy said the 2020 ARTnews interview. And yet, the space would go on to make a substantive mark on 1980s New York.

Steven Parrino, an artist whose punkish paintings defiled the aesthetic purity of the modernist monochrome, had his first solo exhibition with Nature Morte in 1983, the same that Gretchen Bender, a video artist known for stealing televisual material from the airwaves, also made her debut there. Cady Noland, Louise Lawler, Sherrie Levine, Robert Gober, Richard Pettibone, and others of note also showed at Nature Morte early on before its closure in New York in 1988.

Nagy continued working as an artist in the years afterward, eventually shedding his austere black-and-white collage aesthetic to make colorful paintings and installations in the ’90s. And then, for a while, he stopped doing solo exhibitions altogether. There was a 23-year interval between his 1997 Nicole Klagsbrun show and his next New York solo show, which got considerably more notice: a 2020 Jeffrey Deitch exhibition staged in collaboration with Magenta Plains, which now represents Nagy.

At the same time, Nagy was putting down roots in India. In 1992, he relocated to New Delhi; he spent the next five years moving between that city and New York. In 1997, he formally opened Nature Morte in New Delhi.

As Nagy recalled, being an artist with any stake in the market was confusing for many observers. “I am conscious of being penalized for being a dealer: Artists aren’t supposed to be interested in the market (ha ha), and my choice is, apparently, seen by some as opportunistic and manipulative,” he wrote in Artforum in 1999 . He also added, “I prefer the combination of market, media, creativity, and personality that comes together in a gallery.”

Peter Nagy was born in 1959 in Bridgeport, Connecticut. He attended New York’s Parsons School of Design, studying communication design, art history, and theory; he graduated in 1981. During his time at Parsons, he began making works that he described as “large-scale, black-and-white drawings influenced by Futurism.”

He quickly ascended in the New York scene, exhibiting in the 1985 Whitney Biennial via the collective Group Material, whose installations often combined objects produced by others. That same group brought Nagy’s art to the 1987 edition of Documenta in Kassel, Germany.

Today, Nagy is best known as a dealer, with Nature Morte continuing to maintain operations in New Delhi and Mumbai. Its roster today includes giants of Indian art such as Vibha Galhotra, Subodh Gupta, Jitish Kallat, Bharti Kher, Mrinalini Mukherjee, Pushpamala N, and the Raqs Media Collective. Dayanita Singh and Vivan Sundaram also previously showed with Nature Morte. The gallery, a mainstay at fairs ranging from the Armory Show to Frieze, has previously made attempts to broaden its reach, formerly operating branches in Berlin and Calcutta.

Nagy viewed Nature Morte’s Indian iteration as a project born from the impulse toward globalism in the art world. But he also cautioned that such globalism had its downside.

Western curators, he said in a 2010 Art in America interview , “often approach Indian contemporary art with very little knowledge of India itself, so they tend to misinterpret or even ignore artists that may have great relevance to the Indian context but seemingly little to the international context. But, hey, cultural translation is one of the obvious pitfalls of the globalization of the contemporary art world.”

More recently, interest in Nagy’s art of the 1980s has grown, thanks in part to the 2020 Jeffrey Deitch show. “How amazing to discover that Nagy’s early output, which shows the artist’s penchant for mapping transformations wrought by expanded media, increased corporate power, and concentrated flows of capital, felt downright prescient today,” wrote critic Jan Avgikos in his Artforum review of that show. “Like Warhol, Nagy was practically clairvoyant in his observations about art and its commodification, the ballooning culture of the copy, and our ongoing anxieties about authenticity.”

article_text:
“Heated Rivalry” star Connor Storrie is in talks to play the villain opposite Ryan Gosling in Marvel’s “ Ghost Rider ” movie.

Shawn Levy is directing the film, from a script by “Star Wars: Starfighter” screenwriter Jonathan Tropper. “Ghost Rider” is slated to release on July 28, 2028. Levy and Gosling also produce the project alongside Marvel Studios chief Kevin Feige, Louis D’Esposito and Stephen Broussard. Executive producers are Richie Palmer and Jessie Henderson.

Related Stories

Disney Names Carol Choi Asia Pacific President as Luke Kang Retires

Landing a Marvel movie would be a big win for Storrie, who shot to pop culture prominence by starring as Russian hockey hunk Ilya Romanov on “Heated Rivalry.” As the story goes, the Texas native was waiting tables at Laurel Grill in Culver City before being offered that game-changing TV role; he’s since parlayed that attention into a Primetime Emmy-nominated turn as guest host of “Saturday Night Live,” and a supporting role opposite Billie Eilish in Sarah Polley’s “The Bell Jar” movie for Focus Features. The much-anticipated second season of “Heated Rivalry” — which centers on the rivals-to-lovers journey between Storrie’s Ilya and Hudson Williams’ Shane Hollander — is now filming and will premiere on HBO Max next spring. Storrie is represented by CAA, Linden Entertainment, Shelter PR, and Yorn Levine.

As for “Ghost Rider,” the project is coming together quickly, with plans to begin shooting in New York next year. Feige made the surprise announcement about the movie during Marvel’s Hall H presentation at San Diego Comic-Con this summer.

“As you know, this is a character I’ve wanted to play for a very long time,” Gosling told the excited crowd.

For years, Gosling had been Marvel fans’ top choice to star in a “Ghost Rider” movie after Nicolas Cage previously played motorcycle stuntman Johnny Blaze in a 2007 origin story movie and its 2011 sequel. In the comics and those movies, Johnny sells his soul to the devil Mephisto in order to cure his father’s cancer. When the rights reverted to Marvel Studios following those movies, Gabriel Luna played the Robby Reyes version of the character — a younger, Latino man — on the ABC TV show “Agents of S.H.I.E.L.D.”

That said, Marvel has yet to confirm which version of Ghost Rider that Gosling will play, so it’s also unclear which villain Storrie would embody. Mephisto was recently introduced into the MCU, played by Sacha Baron Cohen, in the Disney+ series “Ironheart.”

THR broke news of Storrie’s potential involvement in the film. Marvel Studios does not comment on casting.

article_text:
Lesbian artist Barbara Hammer felt invisible for most of her life. She started making films in the late 1960s, but emerging queer filmmakers often face the same challenges today.

“I really felt her frustration at so many different points,” says Brydie O’Connor , director of “Barbara Forever.”

“We had such wonderful partners, but we were all working overtime on this little movie that could. All the success that we’ve seen with this film hasn’t translated into funding for new projects or making money. I really hope that it will at some point.”

Related Stories

Variety Nominated for 62 Arts & Entertainment Journalism Awards

After screenings at Sundance and Berlinale, O’Connor is bringing the film to Ji.hlava Intl. Documentary Film Festival, where she presented it at the U.S. Docs showcase in 2023.

Produced by A Space Time Films and Killer Films production in co-production with Kartemquin Films, it gained powerful allies in Kristen Stewart and uber-producer Christine Vachon .

“Christine was like: ‘I love that it’s an unconventional approach to an unconventional artist.’ I’m such a fan of her filmography and some of her films are the most groundbreaking queer films I’ve ever seen. That’s what supporting a new generation of queer artists looks like,” notes O’Connor.

Making a film about someone who, despite her influence, isn’t exactly a household name, wasn’t easy.

“We kept hearing: ‘We love your enthusiasm for Barbara Hammer, you emerging lesbian filmmaker. But does that relate to the present day and broader audiences?’”

Hammer passed away in 2019.

“I was wondering: How did she do it all? How did she make over 85 films? How did she archive her entire life in 125 boxes that she eventually sold to Yale? How did she have such a successful relationship towards the end of her life? The complexity of just living, being ambitious and trying to make it happen feels very relatable to me,” she says.

“Now, so many people are being introduced to Barbara and feeling so moved by this film. I’m so grateful for that. It’s such a win to release it, but it was hard to convince people of its place in the market.”

Ironically enough, Hammer’s work often felt ahead of her time. Like today’s influencers, she wasn’t afraid to interview passers-by, film herself or share intimate moments with the camera.

“It feels very contemporary. Barbara started using social media at the end of her life, and she was certainly interested in it. She put herself in the frame as a way to process her feelings and certain situation in her life. She filmed everything.”

But there was a reason behind her methods.

“Barbara had this idea that it would offer insight into how one lesbian, and one woman, navigated the world. In the influencer era, that throughline isn’t necessarily as present. When she was first understanding her sexuality, she had never heard the word ‘lesbian’. This set her on this mission to document everything so that other people could see themselves in her work. I think that was part of her impetus to be so prolific.”

O’Connor started researching Hammer’s work as a student.

“She felt invisible when she was coming out, but she also felt invisible in the film and art world. She felt like she wasn’t getting recognized in the way she thought she should be,” she admits.

Hammer wanted the fame that was eluding her – and she wasn’t afraid to say it.

“When you talk to people who were in the scene or had encountered her, they say: ‘Barbara had a huge personality. She was really pushy, you know.’ I think that’s so human. She knew that she had to overemphasize the importance of her work and her presence. It was about becoming a lesbian icon at a time when the world didn’t really want a lesbian icon.”

Although Hammer made personal, experimental films, she still cared about her audience and wanted to engage with them. Up until her death from cancer.

“Connecting with others through art was really at the core of her practice. It’s also why she loved teaching. I definitely try to take at least a page out of Barbara’s book in that regard,” says O’Connor.

“After one screening, a woman came up to me. She said: ‘I’ve never heard of Barbara Hammer. I’m from Texas and I’m not queer. But I was so moved because my father is at the very end of his life, and he keeps telling our family that he’s at peace. After seeing this movie, I finally understand what he’s saying,’” she recalls.

“That’s been one of the greatest gifts. Just talking to audiences.”

article_text:
Photographers and visual artists worldwide are invited to submit single images and photographic series for the third edition of the Chennai Photo Biennale International Photography Open Call, offering selected artists the opportunity to exhibit their work publicly in Chennai, India.

Open Call:

Submissions are open for Edition 3, 2026–27 of the Chennai Photo Biennale International Photography Open Call, an annual platform inviting photographers and artists worldwide to submit work for consideration by an international jury.

The call is open to anyone, from anywhere, working on any subject, with entries accepted across a wide range of photographic approaches. Applicants may submit either individual photographs or a cohesive photo series. Selected finalists will have their work produced and presented as part of a public exhibition in Chennai.

Institutional Context:

The CPB Foundation, a registered non-profit public trust based in Chennai, India, organises the International Photography Open Call and is dedicated to expanding engagement with photography and the photographic medium.

The Foundation also organises the Chennai Photo Biennale, an international photography festival held every two years in Chennai. Through exhibitions, education and public programmes, its activities create opportunities for photographers and audiences to engage with contemporary photographic practices from India and around the world.

Eligibility and Criteria:

The open call welcomes photographers of any age and from anywhere in the world, from amateur to professional practitioners. Applicants under 18 must provide consent from a parent or guardian. Individual artists, collaborative teams and groups may apply.

Submissions may explore fine art, documentary, portraiture, landscape, conceptual, experimental and other approaches to photography. Work that has previously been exhibited or published is eligible, provided the applicant holds the necessary rights.

Applicants may submit unlimited entries. Photo series must contain a minimum of 10 and a maximum of 20 images and should function as a cohesive body of work. Each submission must be accompanied by a concept note and/or captions.

AI-generated images are not accepted and will be disqualified. Video submissions are also not eligible.

Evaluation Process:

A diverse international jury of photographers, artists, curators, editors, and cultural professionals will review every submission.

The jury assesses entries on artistic merit, originality, technical excellence, and relevance to contemporary photographic discourse.

The 2026–27 jury includes practitioners and cultural figures such as Carine Dolek, Charan Singh, Yumi Goto, Danit Ariel, Katy Hundertmark, Ronny Sen, Sadaf Raza, Aditya Arya, Ana Casas Broda, Bhavna Kakar, Emmeline Yong, Senthil Kumaran, Umah Jacob, Ushmita Sahu, Venket Ram and Vineet Vohra, among others.

Successful applicants are expected to be notified in late December 2026.

Practical Information:

Selected finalists will receive print production and exhibition of their work in Chennai, alongside promotion through CPB’s digital campaigns, social media, email communications and print and digital partnerships. Selected artists will also receive a dedicated online feature through the Open Call website and CPB’s social channels.

Selected works may also be considered for travelling exhibitions and digital presentations at partner festivals. An extended shortlist will be presented digitally at the Open Call exhibition venue.

Submission fees vary according to location and entry type. For residents of India and South Asia, the fee is ₹300 for a single image and ₹700 for a photo series. For applicants from the rest of the world, the listed fees are €8 for a single image and €15 for a photo series. Students in India can apply at reduced rates: ₹100 for a single image and ₹200 for a photo series.

Applicants retain copyright and ownership of their work, while shortlisted and selected participants grant the organisers non-exclusive usage rights for purposes connected to the Open Call, the exhibition, the Chennai Photo Biennale, and related promotion.

Applications and Queries:

Submit applications through the Chennai Photo Biennale International Photography Open Call online platform by 31 October 2026.

Submit images according to the technical specifications in the official rules. Upload single-image entries as JPEG files, and submit photo series as a single ZIP file. Shortlisted photographers will subsequently be asked to provide original camera files and full-resolution processed TIFF files for printing.

Deadline: 31 October 2026 Programme: International Photography Open Call, Edition 3, 2026–27 Organisation: CPB Foundation / Chennai Photo Biennale Location: Chennai, India Eligibility: Open internationally, with no age restriction Categories: Single Image and Photo Series Notification: Late December 2026 Queries: opencall@chennaiphotobiennale.com

For more information, please refer to the official website .

Steve Hilton , the Republican contender for California governor, rolled out a plan Wednesday to revive Hollywood production that includes increased tax credits and state-backed financing for studio repairs.

Hilton, who is trailing Democrat Xavier Becerra in the polls, had previously promised to eliminate the $750 million cap on the state’s film incentive and to include actors’ salaries and other “above the line” costs in the program.

Related Stories

Neon Partners With 'NAZA' Filmmakers, Guardian and MK2 to Bring Prize-Winning Doc to Wider Audiences

Morelia Film Festival Prizes: ‘Six Months in a Pink and Blue Building,’ an 'Expression of Pure, Unbound Beauty,' Wins Top ‘Ojo’ Award

In an expanded plan shared with Variety , Hilton offered additional details and also included an extensive proposal to support soundstage modernization.

Popular on Variety

“No governor can reverse every decision made by an entertainment company, nor should a governor try to micromanage private businesses — or indeed the structure of a fast-changing industry,” the plan states. “But California’s government is responsible for the costs and bureaucracy it imposes on people trying to work here, and for its response to competitive pressures from other places.”

Becerra has issued his own position paper for the entertainment industry, but it is shorter on details. He has refused to be pinned down on whether he would eliminate the cap on the state tax incentive, saying instead that he will wait to see what proposals come out of the state legislature. Both candidates have acknowledged the dramatic downturn in production jobs over the last four years — some 52,000 statewide — and vowed to take steps to address it.

Both are also supportive of a federal film incentive, which was introduced in Congress last month, that would create a 20% tax credit on all U.S. labor costs.

California currently offers a 35% tax credit on all below-the-line costs for films and TV shows that are chosen by the state film commission, with bonuses that go up to 45%. Productions must apply for credits at periodic intervals, and sometimes the program is oversubscribed and unable to accept new applications.

In his plan, Hilton said he will offer a 40% state tax credit for production. He also floated the idea of going as high as 50% for a period of five years. By eliminating the $750 million cap, Hilton also proposes to make California credits automatic, creating stability and predictability for productions, though at an unknown cost.

“Steve will replace narrow application windows with continuous rolling approvals,” the plan states, adding that productions should get an answer within 30 days.

The proposal also includes a sales tax exemption for five years on building materials needed for studio construction, as well as state-backed bond financing for studio acquisition and renovation.

Gov. Gavin Newsom approved a $150 million incentive to boost soundstage construction in 2021. That funding has since been depleted, and there has not yet been a discussion about whether to allocate additional money to it. Los Angeles soundstages are at just 62% occupancy, according to the latest FilmLA report, though new stages continue to open.

Hilton also pledges to include commercials, documentaries and reality TV — all currently excluded from eligibility.

article_text:
Surreale, ma bello. È una delle citazioni iconiche di Notting Hill , il film del 1999 con Hugh Grant e Julia Roberts che ha trasformato un quartiere londinese in uno dei luoghi più riconoscibili del cinema. E adesso torna a far parlare di sé: la casa con la porta blu di William Thacker, il libraio che si innamora di una diva di Hollywood, è in vendita. Prezzo richiesto: 7,5 milioni di sterline.

A proporla è UK Sotheby’s International Realty. Si trova al 280 di Westbourne Park Road e ha una storia architettonica tutt’altro che ordinaria. Prima di diventare una residenza privata, infatti, l’edificio era una cappella battista ottocentesca, trasformata in abitazione nel 1993 dallo sceneggiatore Richard Curtis – proprio l’autore di Notting Hill .

La superficie è di circa 256 metri quadrati, con tre camere da letto e due bagni, ma il vero protagonista è il grande ambiente centrale: quasi 48 piedi di lunghezza, circa 14,6 metri, originariamente concepito come studio d’artista. Il soffitto a volta, le imponenti travi a vista e una serie di lucernari che portano la luce dall’alto ne accentuano le proporzioni quasi da loft. E ancora pavimenti in legno scuro, un camino in pietra e una cucina contemporanea con una grande isola in marmo, che dialoga con la zona pranzo e il soggiorno.

Eppure, guardando le fotografie dell’annuncio, i nostalgici di Notting Hill non potranno fare a meno di pensare a un’altra versione della casa ora in vendita. Quella decisamente meno impeccabile in cui viveva William: piatti e avanzi dei pasti lasciati in giro, un frigorifero sui generis (Albicocche dentro il miele?) , oggetti accumulati e oggetti persi (gli occhiali prima dell’appuntamento al cinema), il divano davanti alla televisione, la vasca da bagno. E soprattutto Spike, l’amabile coinquilino interpretato da Rhys Ifans, con il suo guardaroba improbabile e una concezione dell’ordine decisamente personale. Difficile immaginarlo aggirarsi oggi fra gli ambienti immacolati fotografati da Sotheby’s.

Uno degli elementi più suggestivi è la galleria al primo piano, che corre lungo buona parte del salone e si affaccia sull’ambiente sottostante. Qui trova posto uno studio soppalcato, con pareti attrezzate a libreria e una finestra ad arco con vetri decorati e colorati. Un dettaglio che sembra quasi un omaggio alla vocazione letteraria di William, anche se il libraio cinematografico probabilmente avrebbe riempito quegli scaffali in modo un po’ meno ordinato.

La zona notte comprende una camera padronale al piano superiore, con armadi su misura e un bagno privato dotato di doppio lavabo, doccia separata e vasca freestanding. Altri due ambienti destinati a camera da letto si trovano al piano inferiore, insieme a un secondo bagno con doccia e a un locale lavanderia. Caminetti d’epoca, cornici decorative, pavimenti in legno e vetrate colorate conservano il carattere storico dell’edificio anche negli spazi più privati.

E poi ci sono gli esterni della casa di Notting Hill, tutt’altro che secondari in una proprietà londinese in vendita. Una scala a chiocciola conduce alla terrazza sul tetto, di circa 8,8 per 4,3 metri, protetta da vecchi muri in mattoni e circondata da piante mature, con una bella vista sui tetti di Notting Hill. Sul retro, invece, si apre un cortile-giardino di circa dieci metri, un angolo verde riservato con spazi per sedersi e mangiare all’aperto. Due piccoli rifugi urbani che rendono la casa ancora più interessante.

C’è una precisazione importante, in effetti: la facciata della proprietà fu effettivamente utilizzata nel film, ma gli interni dell’appartamento di William vennero ricostruiti in studio. La casa reale apparteneva a Richard Curtis, che la trasformò da ex cappella in abitazione insieme alla compagna Emma Freud. Anche la celebre porta blu ha una sua storia: quella originale, ottocentesca, fu venduta all’asta per beneficenza dopo il successo del film; quella che si vede oggi è una sostituzione.

Il contrasto è irresistibile. Da una parte una residenza di lusso, con ambienti da galleria d’arte, biblioteca soppalcata e terrazza panoramica nell’annuncio di UK Sotheby’s International Realty ; dall’altra l’appartamento cinematografico in cui sembrava che la vita, con tutto il suo disordine, avesse preso definitivamente il sopravvento. Surreale, ma bello.

article_text:
The ninth edition of Egypt’s El Gouna Film Festival brings together a strong showing of Arab cinema to the Red Sea, with a lineup spanning emerging regional voices, established filmmakers, and prize-winning titles from Cannes, Berlin, Venice, Sundance and Shanghai.

Across its narrative, documentary and short-film competitions, this year’s selection features stories of love, memory and family, as well as war and displacement, while offering glimpses of communities navigating political, social and economic upheaval. Several titles also underscore El Gouna’s growing role in nurturing projects before they reach the screen, with filmmakers and projects previously supported through CineGouna, the festival’s industry arm, returning with completed works.

Related Stories

Lara Croft’s Inaugural Voice Actor Shelley Blond Recalls First Time She Saw ‘Tomb Raider’ Character: ‘I Thought She Was Very Sexy and Very Ballsy’

Vino G. Bastian, Pevita Pearce, Faradina Mufti, Indra Jegel Lead 'Miracle in Cell No. 7' Director Lee Hwan-kyung’s Indonesian Father-Son Drama 'Gasigogi' (EXCLUSIVE)

Here are 10 titles to keep an eye on at this year’s festival.

Popular on Variety

Feature Narrative Competition

“Safe Exit” (2026) (Mohammed Hammad, Egypt, Libya, Tunisia, Qatar, Germany. Produced by Kholoud Saad, Dora Bouchoucha, Dina Farouk, Ibrahim El-Batout, and May Odeh)

A decade after his feature debut, Egyptian filmmaker Mohammed Hammad delivers his sophomore film, “Safe Exit,” which premiered at this year’s Berlinale. Set in downtown Cairo, it centers on Samaan, a Coptic Christian security guard haunted by his father’s murder by extremists, whose life changes when he meets Fatma, an impoverished sex worker facing struggles of her own. Hammad explores faith, isolation, and some of the contradictions of contemporary Egyptian society. His debut, “ Withered Green ,” screened at El Gouna’s inaugural edition in 2017.

“Only Rebels Win” (2026) (Danielle Arbid, France, Lebanon, Qatar. Produced by Omar El Kadi, Nadia Turincev and Georges Schoucair)

Widowed and with her children now grown, Suzanne (Hiam Abbass), a Lebanese woman of Palestinian origin, finds herself free to put herself first. When she falls for Osmane, a younger undocumented Sudanese migrant in Beirut, their relationship puts that newfound independence to the test. When the war made shooting in Lebanon impossible, director Danielle Arbid had a local crew film the Beirut locations without actors, then used the footage as rear projections while shooting in a Paris studio. “Only Rebels Win” opened the Panorama section at this year’s Berlinale.

“ 3 Weeks After ” (2026) (Miroslav Terzić, Serbia, Bulgaria, Italy, Croatia, Luxembourg. Produced by Snežana van Houwelingen and Branislav Trifunović)

Fresh off of winning the Europa Cinemas Label at Karlovy Vary, Miroslav Terzić’s “3 Weeks After” centers on a group of students stranded at an isolated mountain hotel three weeks after a classmate dies by suicide. Questions soon emerge about the bullying that preceded his death, and about how many of them knew what was happening. Rather than concentrating solely on those responsible, Terzić widens the circle to the classmates who were silent bystanders who never intervened.

“ Halima ” (2026) (Yassine El Idrissi, Morocco. Produced by Yassine El Idrissi)

Best director and best actress winner (Khadija Amari) at the Shanghai International Film Festival, “Halima” marks Moroccan filmmaker Yassine El Idrissi’s fiction feature debut. Moving between Halima’s present-day life on the Moroccan coast and her past in the Rif mountains, the film traces how the widow, threatened with displacement from her land and struggling to support herself, became involved in the illegal cannabis trade. Drawing on El Idrissi’s years as a photojournalist and his encounters with marginalized communities across Morocco, “Halima” looks at the region’s hidden cannabis economy while resisting easy judgments about the people whose livelihoods depend on it.

Feature Documentary Competition

“Citizen Osama” (2026) (Ahmed Hassouna, Palestine, France. Produced by Laura Nikolov and Rashid Masharawi. Co-produced by Ahmed Hassouna)

In northern Gaza, photojournalist Osama Al-Ashi is documenting a war while trying to survive it. A Venice premiere, Ahmed Hassouna’s documentary follows Al-Ashi as his work to record the devastation all around him collides with the responsibility of keeping his wife and newborn son out of harm’s way. The film has been selected as Palestine’s official entry for Best International Feature Film at the 2027 Academy Awards.

“The Return of Captain Kabonga” (2026) (Amir El-Shenawy, Egypt. Produced by Ahmed Abdelsalam)

In Ismailia, a city along Egypt’s Suez Canal, veteran street wrestler Ashraf “Kabonga” Mahrous is trying to revive the WWE-inspired wrestling shows he once staged with a group of local amateurs. Amir El-Shenawy tracks that effort alongside Kabonga’s more immediate struggle to make ends meet and support his family while Egypt grapples with economic crisis. “The Return of Captain Kabonga” makes its world premiere at El Gouna after participating in CineGouna Funding in 2025 where the project picked up several cash and in-kind post-production awards.

“ Whispers in May ” (2026) (Dongnan Chen, Hong Kong, Netherlands, South Korea, Sweden. Produced by Jia Zhao and Kay Xu. Co-produced by Heejung Oh and Malin Hüber)

Fourteen-year-old Qihuo gets her first period and sets out with her friends to find a traditional skirt for her coming-of-age ceremony in China’s remote Liangshan Mountains. With her parents away working in the city, her journey captures how life is changing for young people even as long-held customs remain firmly rooted. Blending documentary with fictional and mythical elements, Dongnan Chen’s “Whispers in May” won the top DOX:AWARD at this year’s CPH:DOX.

“ Nuisance Bear ” (2026) (Gabriela Osio Vanden and Jack Weisman, Canada, U.S., U.K. Produced by Michael Code, Teddy Leifer and Will N. Miller)

Winner of the Grand Jury Prize in the U.S. Documentary Competition at Sundance, “Nuisance Bear” follows polar bears along their centuries-old migration route through Manitoba, Canada, where they increasingly cross paths with tourists, wildlife officers and hunters. Directors Gabriela Osio Vanden and Jack Weisman expand their Oscar-shortlisted 2021 short of the same name into a feature that shifts the usual nature-documentary perspective, showing the bears’ migration from their point of view, with humans and the town itself becoming the intruders.

Short Film Competition

“My Village Blamed Women for the End of Mankind” (Al Khabith) (2026) (Jad Chahine, Egypt, United Kingdom. Produced by Yara Goubran)

When a mysterious epidemic begins infecting women in a remote fishing village, fear quickly turns the community against them. “At its core, the film is about a man trying to protect three women from death, only to discover that protection itself can become part of the violence inflicted upon them,” director Jad Chahine explains. That contradiction feeds into a larger question Chahine poses to the audience, and perhaps to himself: “If the end is inevitable, what gives us the right to decide when it begins? And when does our fear of it make us create it with our own hands?” Making its world premiere at El Gouna, the film follows Chahine’s Cannes La Cinef-selected “The Call of the Brook.”

“Disquiet” (Irtibak) (2026) (Mariam Abdelgaber, Egypt. Produced by Tamer Ashry, Zeina Eissa, Alia El Shahbour and Mariam Abdelgaber)

A young supermarket cashier is given a key by an elderly regular who asks her to check on her apartment if she ever disappears. When the woman stops coming to the store, the cashier decides to use it, drawing her into the private life of someone she barely knew. “Disquiet” marks Mariam Abdelgaber’s debut in narrative filmmaking and stars Rakeen Saad and Menha El Batraoui. The film makes its world premiere at El Gouna.

article_text:
Dal 21 marzo 2027 Palazzo Grassi cambierà funzione e diventerà la sede permanente della Collezione Pinault a Venezia . Dopo 20 anni di mostre temporanee, il palazzo sul Canal Grande ospiterà in modo stabile oltre cento opere scelte dalla raccolta di François Pinault , in un percorso curato da Emma Lavigne , direttrice e conservatrice generale della Collezione, insieme all’équipe curatoriale di Pinault Collection.

È una trasformazione significativa nell’assetto del progetto veneziano, con Punta della Dogana che continuerà a ospitare grandi mostre temporanee, monografiche o tematiche, e il Teatrino che manterrà il proprio ruolo come spazio per cinema, performance, incontri e ricerca.

Il progetto culturale di Pinault riparte – ancora – da Venezia

L’avventura veneziana di Pinault iniziò nel 2006, con la riapertura di Palazzo Grassi dopo l’intervento di Tadao Ando . Tre anni più tardi arrivò Punta della Dogana, ancora su progetto dell’architetto giapponese, seguita dal Teatrino e, nel 2021, dalla Bourse de Commerce di Parigi.

In 20 anni, Palazzo Grassi ha ospitato 27 mostre, parallelamente, la Collezione Pinault è cresciuta fino a superare le 10mila opere di arte moderna e contemporanea, distribuite tra linguaggi, generazioni e aree geografiche differenti. La nuova presentazione permanente nasce quindi dall’esigenza di dare maggiore visibilità a una parte di questo patrimonio, rendendo più leggibili nel tempo le relazioni tra artisti e opere che fino a oggi sono emerse soltanto attraverso mostre temporanee.

«Ho sempre pensato che fosse necessario dare tempo alle opere: il tempo di essere viste, riviste e talvolta comprese sotto una luce diversa», ha spiegato François Pinault. «A vent’anni dall’apertura di Palazzo Grassi, ho voluto dare ad alcune di esse una collocazione duratura. Non per cristallizzare la Collezione, ma per permettere alle opere di continuare a interrogarci e rinnovare il nostro sguardo sul mondo».

Dall’ultimo palazzo patrizio sul Canal Grande alle grandi mostre

Prima di diventare una delle principali sedi veneziane dedicate all’arte contemporanea, Palazzo Grassi ha attraversato quasi tre secoli di trasformazioni. Affacciato sul Canal Grande, nel sestiere di San Marco, viene generalmente ricordato come l’ultimo grande palazzo patrizio costruito a Venezia prima della caduta della Serenissima.

La famiglia Grassi iniziò ad acquistare progressivamente gli edifici e i terreni dell’area a partire dal 1732. La costruzione del nuovo palazzo viene fatta risalire alla metà del Settecento: i lavori sarebbero iniziati intorno al 1748 e si sarebbero conclusi entro il 1772. All’interno, lo scalone d’onore fu decorato con affreschi di Michelangelo Morlaiter e Francesco Zanchi .

Con l’estinzione della famiglia Grassi, nell’Ottocento l’edificio passò rapidamente attraverso diversi proprietari. Nel 1857 fu acquistato dal finanziere greco Simone de Sina , che intervenne in maniera consistente sugli ambienti, modificando anche la sala da ballo e parte delle decorazioni settecentesche.

Nel 1908 il palazzo passò all’industriale svizzero Giovanni Stucky e successivamente al figlio Gian Carlo, che vi introdusse ascensori, impianti elettrici e riscaldamento. Ma è soprattutto dalla metà del Novecento che Palazzo Grassi comincia ad assumere una funzione culturale sempre più marcata.

Nel 1949 l’edificio passò a una società immobiliare legata alla Snia Viscosa. Sotto l’impulso di Franco Marinotti nacque qui il Centro Internazionale dell’Arte e del Costume, portando nel palazzo mostre e manifestazioni culturali. Tra il 1951 e il 1958 furono organizzate importanti esposizioni dedicate all’arte e al costume. Successivamente, con Paolo Marinotti, l’attenzione si concentrò sempre più sull’arte contemporanea, con mostre dedicate anche ad artisti come Asger Jorn, Max Ernst e Jean Dubuffet .

Un nuovo passaggio decisivo arrivò nel 1983, quando Palazzo Grassi fu acquistato dalla Fiat. La ristrutturazione venne affidata a Gae Aulenti , che adeguò gli ambienti alle esigenze espositive contemporanee, intervenendo sugli impianti e sull’organizzazione interna senza cancellarne l’identità storica. Da allora il palazzo consolidò definitivamente il proprio ruolo come sede per grandi esposizioni internazionali.

Oltre cento opere in un percorso permanente

Il nuovo allestimento riunirà 106 opere considerate punti di riferimento della Collezione, così da costruire relazioni più profonde e cogliere nuove corrispondenze. Ad aprire il percorso sarà un’opera di Mario Merz , scelta non casuale per sottolineare il legame di Pinault con l’arte italiana e in particolare con l’Arte Povera, movimento presente in maniera significativa nella raccolta. Ci sarà poi Him di Maurizio Cattelan , oltre a lavori di Anne Imhof , Anicka Yi e Lucas Arruda , mentre nell’atrio del Palazzo saranno ospitate grandi installazioni, come un’opera specchiante di Kimsooja che interverrà nella percezione dello spazio architettonico e nelrapporto tra visitatore e ambiente.

L’idea di una sede permanente non comporterà però l’immobilizzazione del percorso. Le opere potranno essere reinterpretate e riallestite, mentre nuove acquisizioni continueranno ad ampliare una raccolta che Pinault considera per definizione in divenire.

A Punta della Dogana, Tadao Ando e Mono-ha

Mentre Palazzo Grassi inaugurerà il nuovo corso della Collezione Pinault, sempre il 21 marzo 2027 Punta della Dogana dedicherà una mostra a Tadao Ando , celebrando anche il rapporto che da circa 25 anni lega l’architetto giapponese a François Pinault. Una collaborazione dalla quale sono nati gli interventi per Palazzo Grassi nel 2006, Punta della Dogana nel 2009, il Teatrino nel 2013 e la Bourse de Commerce di Parigi nel 2021.

Tadao Ando e Mono-Ha. I cinque elementi sarà incentrata su un aspetto meno noto della pratica dell’architetto: la fotografia. Diverse centinaia di immagini realizzate dallo stesso Ando, alcune presentate per la prima volta, ricostruiranno il suo modo di osservare le proprie architetture e di interrogare il rapporto tra costruzione, immagine ed esperienza dello spazio.

Cinque elementi guideranno il percorso: aria, intesa attraverso il vuoto e il concetto giapponese di ma ; terra, legata al contesto e alla storia; acqua, associata alla fluidità; fuoco, come elemento di trasformazione di materiali quali vetro e metallo; e calcestruzzo, materiale centrale nel linguaggio architettonico di Ando.

La mostra metterà queste ricerche in relazione con Mono-ha, la «Scuola delle cose» nata in Giappone alla fine degli anni Sessanta intorno ad artisti come Nobuo Sekine , Kishio Suga , Lee Ufan e Jiro Takamatsu . Attraverso materiali essenziali e interventi ridotti al minimo, il movimento concentrò l’attenzione sulle relazioni tra materia, spazio e percezione. Pinault Collection conserva oggi una delle raccolte più rilevanti di opere Mono-ha al di fuori del Giappone.

article_text:
EXCLUSIVE: Celine Dion will perform original songs written and composed by Paul McCartney for the upcoming 3D animated feature High in the Clouds , adapted from his children’s novel, with the soundtrack to be released worldwide by Universal Music Group.

Related Stories

Céline Dion Family TV Series In The Works

Sam Mendes’ Beatles Biopic Recreates ‘Abbey Road’ Album Cover In Behind-The-Scenes Video — Watch

Dion already has been announced as member of the voice cast topped by Himesh Patel and Hannah Waddingham and also featuring McCartney, Idris Elba, Lionel Richie, Ringo Starr and Jimmy Fallon, among many others.

Waddingham, Patel and McCartney also will lend their voices to original musical performances throughout the picture.

RELATED: The 30 Highest-Grossing Animated Films Of All Time At The Global Box Office

Watch on Deadline

High in the Clouds follows the adventures of teenage squirrel Wirral (Patel) as he accidentally sparks a revolution against Gretsch (Waddingham), the bossy diva-owl who has banned all music from his town, and embarks on an extraordinary journey to set music free. Dion voices Wirral’s mother, Sugartail.

Up Oscar winner Michael Giacchino, who also worked on Ratatouille, Inside Out, Coco, Klara and the Sun and many others, has composed the original score based on McCartney themes.

News that Dion is recording the original songs comes just 10 days after “The Power of Love” singer completed the first of her comeback concert residency in Paris, which drew some 550,000 spectators across 16 shows.

It was Dion’s first major concert program since being forced to abandon her Courage World Tour in 2020 due to the pandemic, followed by health struggles.

McCartney posted about his joy at seeing Dion back on the concert circuit on social media back in September.

“It’s been so great to see the amazing reaction to Céline’s comeback in Paris. There’s so much love out there for her,” he wrote.

“I’m so excited that she’s part of our High in the Clouds film. I’ve just been listening to some of her parts, and I’m blown away by it. Wow, what a talent. We are very lucky to have her as part of the team. Can’t wait to share it with the world.”

High in the Clouds is adapted from McCartney’s 2005 novel, co-written with Philip Ardagh and illustrated by Geoff Dunbar. An earlier iteration of the animated film dating back to 2015 saw the Beatles star McCartney collaborate briefly with Lady Gaga on one of the tracks.

The picture is directed by animation filmmaker Toby Genkel ( The Amazing Maurice ) from a screenplay by Oscar winner Jon Crocker ( Paddington 2 ), with production design by Patrick Hanenberger ( Rise of the Guardians , The Lego Movie 2 ).

The film is produced by McCartney (MPL Communications), Robert Shaye and Michael Lynne (Unique Features), and by Sidonie Dumas, Nicolas Atlan, and Terry Kalagian for Gaumont, in association with MPL Communications, Michele Anthony and David Blackman for Polygram Entertainment, Lemoko Investments, Sky, and James L. Nederlander Productions.

Award-winning Gaumont Animation is producing the feature and partnering with the team at 88 Pictures ( The Bad Guys: A Very Bad Holiday, Spirit Untamed ), which is handling key animation elements of the film.

Gaumont will present an exclusive work-in-progress screening of High in the Clouds during the upcoming American Film Market ( AFM ).

The film already has been sold in major territories to UK (Sky UK Ltd.), German-speaking territories (Constantin Film), Eastern Europe (Vertical/Monolith/AQS), Latin America (Imagem), CIS (Mint Films), Middle East (Four Star), South-East Asia/Taiwan/HK (A Really Good Film), Greece (Tanweer), Portugal (Cinemundo), Israel (Lev), Baltics (Acme), South Africa (Sun)

CAA Media Finance is handling North America

article_text:
Former A24 docs chief Nicole Stott has joined Magna Studios , the production outfit behind Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger.

Stott becomes an executive producer in Magna’s non-fiction division and will collaborate closely with SVP, Non-Fiction, Oliver Calleja, Creative Director Louis Mole, and the wider team across Magna’s documentary features and limited series.

A24 shuttered its documentary hub last year but prior to this Stott had been division head, working across the likes of The Yogurt Shop Murders and Sundance Grand Jury Prize-winner Nuisance Bear . A24 was in production on smash Elizabeth Holmes doc You Can See Everything at the time, although she didn’t work directly across the movie. She is a former co-head of non fiction at Concordia Studio and headed up London’s Passion Pictures docs for a decade.

Magna Studios is run by former Pulse Films execs Marisa Clifford and Davud Karbassioun, and is owned by Lumina Media , the next-gen company founded by Pulse founder Thomas Benski.

Watch on Deadline

It has made the likes of Disney+’s Oasis: Don’t Look Back in Anger , Sky’s The Pembrokeshire Murders and the upcoming Lily Allen feature for Prime Video.

Clifford said: “Nicole is a perfect fit for the world-class team we’ve assembled here at Magna. Her outstanding body of work and creative vision make her an invaluable asset as we push boundaries and scale our studio globally.”

title_original: 《鏡子》：在夢境與回憶的現實裡，我常說妳像我的母親
title_zh: 《鏡子》：在夢境與回憶的現實裡，我常說妳像我的母親
summary_zh: 来源摘录：在 1975 年的電影《鏡子》（The Mirror）中，俄國導演安德烈・塔可夫斯基（Andrey Tarkovskiy）選擇重塑慣常的線性時間概念，不以因果關係為邏輯、大量動用情感記憶為敘事基底的習慣，也為塔可夫斯基對「電影是被記錄下的時間」的思考，於是《鏡子》也能視為他對記憶的復刻。 這篇文章 《鏡子》：在夢境與回憶的現實裡，我常說妳像我的母親 最早出現於 釀電影 。
article_blocks_json: [{"type": "quote", "text": "讀者投稿／徐悦溪 劇照來源／IMDb 責任編輯／黃曦 核稿編輯／黃曦"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "編按：發表於 1975 年的電影《鏡子》（The Mirror），是二十世紀最負盛名的俄國導演 安德烈・塔可夫斯基（Andrey Tarkovskiy，1932－1986） 的代表名作之一。極具自傳性色彩的電影，透過阿列克謝（Alexei）的夢境、回憶與現實等元素不斷地交織，以此勾勒出主角的過去童年與當前生活，這些都極大程度地來自塔可夫斯基自身的回憶。", "links": [{"text": "安德烈・塔可夫斯基（Andrey Tarkovskiy，1932－1986）", "url": "https://filmaholic.tw/films/5fe1c6d4fd89780001f3baa6/"}]}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《鏡子》打破傳統的敘事結構，或說是心之所欲地依賴當下的主觀感受，而非以邏輯的敘事展開；有人曾評論「塔克斯夫斯基不是個簡單的即興大師，確切地說，他應該是一個造物主。在加工物質和鑄造人物模型的同時，他將空間和時間澈底重組。」（註 1）而《鏡子》則更進一步加工其中之意象，串連起線性時間之外、在一般世界已然斷裂的時空，僅僅真誠地傳達著塔可夫斯基的情感與思考。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "本文將藉由分析時間的重塑、意象的串連所搭建之敘事結構，嘗試論集電影如何在最終指向塔可夫斯及，以及其之於自身生命的思考。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/BDI2EN48iwGSVAf0RBdFyxy4HLw7Fk105x0Tv0O6TpM/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/bdb1e400-5144-4251-8815-d2daf136c64e.png", "alt": "《鏡子》電影劇照／劇照來源：IMDb", "caption": "", "credit": "釀電影"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《鏡子》電影劇照／劇照來源：IMDb"}, {"type": "heading", "text": "一、敘事基礎：時間的重塑"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在《鏡子》中，塔可夫斯基選擇重塑慣常的線性時間概念，不以因果關係為邏輯、大量動用情感記憶為敘事基底的習慣，也為塔可夫斯基對「電影」的思考──他認為電影是被記錄下的時間──於是《鏡子》也能視為塔可夫斯基對記憶的復刻。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "電影透過突然出現的大火、坍塌的屋頂、消失的女人、黑白的戰爭等記憶進行拼接，讓觀眾難以用連貫的解讀方式理解這部電影，但記憶本就無序、無邏輯，塔可夫斯基選擇藉由形式接近記憶之本質，以此嘗試更大程度地還原記憶本身。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在畫面色彩的處理上，可說是最直接的「提示」。塔可夫斯基曾說道， 「在《鏡子》中，我用黑白、棕褐、低飽和彩色的交替，來表現不同層次的時間與記憶──過去、現在、夢境、潛意識，它們不是線性排列，而是同時並存於意識之中。」（註 2） 色彩的交叉運用，是對主觀記憶的交叉呈現。兒時的田園回憶，導演多用低飽和墨綠、深棕等色調呈現；在電影開頭的畫面，母親的背影被綠色田園包圍，真實的田園時光在塔可夫斯基心中仍是柔和的。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "其後，接踵而至的夢境則以黑白影像呈現，洗頭的母親渾身濕漉，天花板的牆突然坍塌，內心深處的不安赤裸裸地以黑白夢境傳遞，而長大後與妻子對話的畫面，又運用了更多的冷色調。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "夫妻之間的爭吵稱不上激烈，但冷色調與硬光的運用，依舊讓人感受到彼此疏遠的距離。色彩區分的是塔可夫斯基的心理時間，顏色構建出多層次記憶的語言，引導觀眾的思緒隨著塔可夫斯基的主觀時間遊走。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "時間隨著主觀記憶被重組，也能夠透過鏡頭被拉長，《鏡子》透過長鏡頭描繪綿延的時光感。 屋外著火，兩個孩子也起身走出畫面、跑到外面，鏡頭就在空蕩蕩的餐桌上，幾乎難以察覺地、緩慢向後移動整整十秒，直到桌上的花瓶被風吹倒，發出清脆的響聲，鏡頭才轉向一面鏡子，鏡子中是童年主角和妹妹，正在眺望那場大火。"}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "童年的世界很小，對於自己感官之外的事物總是難以察覺，而再次回望過去，塔可夫斯基對周遭事物的記錄與捕捉，綿延著記憶的時光。"}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://img.vocus.cc/LXwgEWos_XCwG_SI5uR5DaeS9Bbl-K4e2eI6mbKbxPA/w:740/f:jpg/plain/https://images.vocus.cc/417ee036-c345-4870-8877-569af11ffa09.png", "alt": "《鏡子》電影劇照／劇照來源：IMDb", "caption": "", article_text:
讀者投稿／徐悦溪 劇照來源／IMDb 責任編輯／黃曦 核稿編輯／黃曦

編按：發表於 1975 年的電影《鏡子》（The Mirror），是二十世紀最負盛名的俄國導演 安德烈・塔可夫斯基（Andrey Tarkovskiy，1932－1986） 的代表名作之一。極具自傳性色彩的電影，透過阿列克謝（Alexei）的夢境、回憶與現實等元素不斷地交織，以此勾勒出主角的過去童年與當前生活，這些都極大程度地來自塔可夫斯基自身的回憶。

《鏡子》打破傳統的敘事結構，或說是心之所欲地依賴當下的主觀感受，而非以邏輯的敘事展開；有人曾評論「塔克斯夫斯基不是個簡單的即興大師，確切地說，他應該是一個造物主。在加工物質和鑄造人物模型的同時，他將空間和時間澈底重組。」（註 1）而《鏡子》則更進一步加工其中之意象，串連起線性時間之外、在一般世界已然斷裂的時空，僅僅真誠地傳達著塔可夫斯基的情感與思考。

本文將藉由分析時間的重塑、意象的串連所搭建之敘事結構，嘗試論集電影如何在最終指向塔可夫斯及，以及其之於自身生命的思考。

《鏡子》電影劇照／劇照來源：IMDb

一、敘事基礎：時間的重塑

在《鏡子》中，塔可夫斯基選擇重塑慣常的線性時間概念，不以因果關係為邏輯、大量動用情感記憶為敘事基底的習慣，也為塔可夫斯基對「電影」的思考──他認為電影是被記錄下的時間──於是《鏡子》也能視為塔可夫斯基對記憶的復刻。

電影透過突然出現的大火、坍塌的屋頂、消失的女人、黑白的戰爭等記憶進行拼接，讓觀眾難以用連貫的解讀方式理解這部電影，但記憶本就無序、無邏輯，塔可夫斯基選擇藉由形式接近記憶之本質，以此嘗試更大程度地還原記憶本身。

在畫面色彩的處理上，可說是最直接的「提示」。塔可夫斯基曾說道， 「在《鏡子》中，我用黑白、棕褐、低飽和彩色的交替，來表現不同層次的時間與記憶──過去、現在、夢境、潛意識，它們不是線性排列，而是同時並存於意識之中。」（註 2） 色彩的交叉運用，是對主觀記憶的交叉呈現。兒時的田園回憶，導演多用低飽和墨綠、深棕等色調呈現；在電影開頭的畫面，母親的背影被綠色田園包圍，真實的田園時光在塔可夫斯基心中仍是柔和的。

其後，接踵而至的夢境則以黑白影像呈現，洗頭的母親渾身濕漉，天花板的牆突然坍塌，內心深處的不安赤裸裸地以黑白夢境傳遞，而長大後與妻子對話的畫面，又運用了更多的冷色調。

夫妻之間的爭吵稱不上激烈，但冷色調與硬光的運用，依舊讓人感受到彼此疏遠的距離。色彩區分的是塔可夫斯基的心理時間，顏色構建出多層次記憶的語言，引導觀眾的思緒隨著塔可夫斯基的主觀時間遊走。

時間隨著主觀記憶被重組，也能夠透過鏡頭被拉長，《鏡子》透過長鏡頭描繪綿延的時光感。 屋外著火，兩個孩子也起身走出畫面、跑到外面，鏡頭就在空蕩蕩的餐桌上，幾乎難以察覺地、緩慢向後移動整整十秒，直到桌上的花瓶被風吹倒，發出清脆的響聲，鏡頭才轉向一面鏡子，鏡子中是童年主角和妹妹，正在眺望那場大火。

童年的世界很小，對於自己感官之外的事物總是難以察覺，而再次回望過去，塔可夫斯基對周遭事物的記錄與捕捉，綿延著記憶的時光。

《鏡子》電影劇照／劇照來源：IMDb

二、敘事紐帶：意象的串聯

在《鏡子》的敘事結構中，水、火、鏡子等核心意象反覆出現，串聯起不同時間層的敘事紐帶，在碎片化的記憶之間建立起隱秘的聯結，使主觀情感得以在非線性的敘事中流動。

水，似乎總與母親聯繫在一起。第一個夢境，父親幫母親洗頭；鏡頭一轉，只剩下母親一人，屋頂開始漏水，天花板坍塌，母親濕漉漉地獨自行走；緊接著，母親的電話響起，另一段回憶隨之而來，母親冒雨奔跑、去檢查工作的失誤；又或者是，母親操勞之時，溪水在一旁緩緩地流淌。水串聯起的母親形象，時而傷感，時而猛烈，時而溫柔，卻始終滋養著他。

火，象徵著燃燒不盡的生命力。它總與塔可夫斯基的成長聯繫在一起，童年目睹屋外的火災，後續的現實又問到，父親的離開是不是也在大火那年；串聯起童年記憶與電影敘事，於是孩子開始學會面對離開；又或是在母親去鄰居家求助時，孩子望向火爐，看到初戀在火爐旁取暖，青年記憶勾連出來，就連中年主角的回憶視角，也看到了他的孩子在窗外燒火。童年、青年、中年的碎片化敘事，皆以火的出現聯結時間的流動。

《鏡子》電影劇照／劇照來源：IMDb

鏡子，則串聯起過去與現在。不難發現《鏡子》中的母親與妻子、年幼主角與長大所生的兒子，是同一個演員。在妻子的第一次出現，她望向巨大鏡子裡的自己，主角的畫外音響起： 「我常說妳像我母親。」

選角本身也是「鏡子」意象的延伸，隱喻著兩代命運的重疊。除此之外，在第一個夢境中，年輕的母親走進屋內的落地鏡，年邁的母親凝視著年輕的自己，而年輕的母親提前看見了衰老，時間折疊進到鏡子裡頭，串聯起同一個體的不同時間態。（註 3）

《鏡子》電影劇照／劇照來源：IMDb

三、叙事落點：塔可夫斯基的生命思考

在重建時間與意象串聯的共同作用下，敘事結構的最終落點，是塔可夫斯基對自身生命的思考與回應。電影開頭運用紀錄片式的長鏡頭，拍攝一位醫生正在治療口吃少年的畫面，在醫生的引導下，少年流利且響亮地說出：「我能說話了。」

這是塔可夫斯基借少年之口，開啟他的自白，他不再膽怯，而是將鏡頭轉向他的內心，「（一個女清潔工）她跟我們說：『一切很簡單，有個人病了，怕死，突然回想起自己給別人造成的痛苦，他想要贖罪，祈求寬恕。』這個女人頭腦簡單，但她全看懂了，她抓住了電影所說的悔恨。」（註 4），這份深埋於內心的悔恨，坦誠地呈現在銀幕之上。

母親的形象在其中反覆出現，不論是在童年回憶中，鏡頭對準母親望著遠方而流下的淚水，還是黑白影像下母親冒雨跑進印刷廠、擔心工作失誤帶來的嚴重後果，看似沒有關聯的記憶拼接，都在向觀眾展現母親在家庭的堅忍與付出。

回望過去，塔可夫斯基看見母親的苦苦等待、犧牲和隱忍，這種鏡頭下的「看見」本身就是一種表達，是他對母親遲來的愧疚與懺悔。

不過，塔可夫斯基的生命思考不止於此。當母親與父親走向分離，他與妻子也走向分離，塔可夫斯基的成長要面臨父親的缺席，他兒子的成長也將面臨他這個父親的缺席。破裂與離開的傷害重演，他的生命思考，也是對不斷上演的分離與缺席、對循環往復的代際創傷而悔恨。

《鏡子》電影劇照／劇照來源：IMDb

當主角生命進入到尾聲，他放飛手中的小鳥，新的生命彷彿再次流轉；鏡頭一轉，電影又回到了曾經，年輕的母親和父親躺在草坪上，父親問母親，「想要男孩還是女孩」，母親不語，只是向樹叢後看，看到年邁的自己牽著兒時的主角與妹妹在平原上行走。童年的他，最後向遠方發出一聲有力的吶喊，時空結構再次被打破，病床上的他用主觀記憶勾勒出超現實的相遇，那聲有力的吶喊，便是他借童年之口對年邁母親說出的懺悔。（註 5）

《鏡子》的敘事結構，歸根結底是塔可夫斯基為自我審視而搭建的影像容器。從時間重塑、意象串聯、生命思考，承載著導演對自身生命的回望與懺悔，

而核心意象反覆貫穿於斷裂的時空之間，每一次的重現，都在碎片之間架起情感的橋樑。最終，這一切敘事手段，都指向塔可夫斯基最深層的生命思考，站在畫面之外，審視無法改變的過去，塔可夫斯基對一切的思考，其實都在銀幕之上。

《鏡子》電影劇照／劇照來源：IMDb

註 1.《安德烈・塔可夫斯基》Antoine de Baecque 著，方爾平譯；北京，北京大學出版社，2011。頁 47。

註 2.《雕刻時光》安德烈・塔可夫斯基著，陳麗貴譯；臺北，臺北書林出版有限公司，1993 年。頁 158。

註 3. 〈塔可夫斯基《鏡子》的隱喻意義分析〉孫昊楠著，《寫作》2018 年第 1 期，頁 62 - 65。

註 4.《安德烈・塔可夫斯基》Antoine de Baecque 著，方爾平譯；北京，北京大學出版社，2011。頁 149。

註 5.〈安德烈・塔可夫斯基電影中的言語與失語現象〉周偉智著，《思考者》，頁 74 - 77。
excerpt_original: 在 1975 年的電影《鏡子》（The Mirror）中，俄國導演安德烈・塔可夫斯基（Andrey Tarkovskiy）選擇重塑慣常的線性時間概念，不以因果關係為邏輯、大量動用情感記憶為敘事基底的習慣，也為塔可夫斯基對「電影是被記錄下的時間」的思考，於是《鏡子》也能視為他對記憶的復刻。 這篇文章 《鏡子》：在夢境與回憶的現實裡，我常說妳像我的母親 最早出現於 釀電影 。

article_text:
Films and events

Love

Flies

Moscas

Fernando Eimbcke’s fifth feature, a gentle black-and-white comedy set in a gloriously retro-feel Mexico City, sees an unlikely friendship emerge between a cantankerous landlady and her unexpected tenant.

Screening dates and booking

Check which tickets are still available across the festival – and find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Credits

Director Fernando Eimbcke

Screenwriters Vanesa Garnica, Fernando Eimbcke

With Teresa Sánchez, Bastian Escobar, Hugo Ramírez

Mexico 2026. 99min

Courtesy of Alpha Violet

Language Spanish With English subtitles

Introduction

Olga is not having the best of times. To obtain some extra cash, she decides to rent a room to Tulio, one of the relatives of a cancer patient at the nearby hospital, unaware of the fact that that he is also sneaking his young son into the accommodation. Eimbcke’s wonderful film is a witty companion piece to Duck Season, his engaging feature debut.

Maria Delgado

With thanks to Embassy of Mexico in the United Kingdom.

How to book

Tickets start from £10 for all screenings and events in London, with concessions available for many screenings. Booking information and ticket prices .

For non-Members we charge £1 per ticket for online and phone bookings, up to £3 per transaction. There’s no booking fee if you buy tickets at the box office.

If you’re aged 16 to 25, sign up for free to BFI 25 and Under for a chance to get £6 tickets (without booking fees) to all screenings and events, subject to availability.

Missed out?

More tickets may become available for these screenings before and during the festival. Find out about extra ticket releases and standby queues .

Our programmers recommend...

La Perra

Acclaimed Chilean director Dominga Sotomayor delivers a beautifully shot character-driven study of dependency, loneliness and the complex relationship between past and present.

The Meltdown

Sutherland Award winner Manuela Martelli delivers a knife-edge thriller centring on the disappearance of a teenager in a remote Chilean resort.

Isabel

Gabe Klinger’s film, shot on 16mm, is a gentle, warm and beautifully observed love letter to the pleasures of wine.

article_text:
ポータル：アフロアジア 2026年10月16日（金）–11月29日（日） The 5th Floor（台東区池之端3-3-9花園アレイ 5F） https://the5thfloor.org/ 開館時間：13:00–20:00（最終入場19:30） 休館日：火、水 入場料：500円 企画：岩田智哉（The 5th Floor ディレクター）

The 5th Floorでは、韓国の 東豆川 を拠点に活動するアーティスト・コレクティブ、 AfroAsia Collective （アフロアジア・コレクティヴ）の展覧会「ポータル：アフロアジア」を開催する。 AfroAsia Collective は、キュレーターの サン・ア・ムーン （1985年韓国・ソウル生まれ）とアーティスト・映画作家の チェ・ウォンジュン （1979年韓国・ソウル生まれ）によって2021年に設立された、アフリカおよびアジアの移民コミュニティと関わりながら活動するアーティスト・コレクティブ。1955年にインドネシアのバンドンでアジア・アフリカの29カ国が集まり、植民地主義に反対し連帯を掲げたアジア・アフリカ会議（バンドン会議）の精神を受け継ぎ、東豆川の「Space AfroAsia」を拠点に、現代美術をとおしてアフリカとアジアのあいだの新たな文化的連帯の形成を目指している。これまでのプロジェクトに、ナイジェリアのミュージシャンOsinachiとの音楽コラボレーション（2021–2023）、韓国におけるアフリカ出身者のコミュニティを探るドキュメンタリー《Dongducheon New Town》（2023）、韓国の若者とアフリカ出身の移民の若者がともに取り組むK-popプロジェクト《AfroZia》（2024）などがある。また、グループ展「 PANORAMA 」（ソンウン・アートスペース、ソウル、2025）に参加し、リウム美術館の連続プログラム「 Prime Meridian Unconference 」（ソウル、2025）でトークを行なったほか、カリフォルニア大学デービス校マネッティ・シュレム美術館（2024）、ニューヨーク大学アフリカ・アフリカン・ディアスポラ研究センター（CSAAD、2025）、ハーバード大学（2025）のパブリック・プログラムで作品が上映・紹介されている。

韓国における米軍基地村は、長年にわたり冷戦をめぐる地政学とその軍事秩序によって形づくられてきた。しかし今日、これらの場所は、アフリカ出身の移民コミュニティにとって、新たな移住、定住、文化交流の空間へと変容しつつある。本展は、米軍基地村として知られる東豆川の 保山洞 と 坡州 に焦点を当て、歴史記録やアーカイブ資料、地域のコミュニティの人々のポートレート、ストリートや日常の風景を捉えた写真をとおして、軍事的な必要性から形成された空間が、新たな社会関係やコミュニティの生まれる場へと変化していく過程をたどる。 タイトルにある「ポータル」とは、異なる場所と時間、歴史と経験が交差し、新たな関係が生まれる通路を指す。本展は「アフロアジア・フューチャリズム」を、アフリカとアジアの美学の単純な融合ではなく、植民地主義、軍事化、排除という歴史の交差をもつアフリカとアジアのあいだの連帯から、新たな共同性と未来を生み出すための方法論および実践として提示しようとする。

article_text:
大阪・関西万博のシグネチャーパビリオン「null²」の体験を再構成した常設シアター 「null²ⁿ（ﾇﾙﾇﾙネクサス）」 が10月14日、横浜ランドマークタワー・ランドマークプラザ5階に開業する。

メディアアーティストの落合陽一が手がける「null²」は、特殊なミラー膜やLED、ロボティクスなどを組み合わせ、建築や映像、立体物が一体となった体験型パビリオンとして話題を集めた。今回オープンする「null²ⁿ」は、その建物を再現するのではなく、万博での体験を常設シアターとして再構成するプロジェクト。2つのLEDシアターを含む全5室を約60分かけて巡り、光や鏡、音、映像を通じた没入体験を楽しめる。

入口となる「門」には、万博の「null²」でも印象的だった、丸いLEDを組み込んだ「目玉LED」が登場。そこから始まる5つのエリアでは、それぞれ異なる空間体験が展開される。

最初の「壱の間」は「さよならホモサピエンス」と題したエリア。鏡面の反射によって映像と空間が溶け合う、視覚的な演出が特徴だ。続く「弐の間」は「無眼界の夢」。映像や光を極限まで抑えた無響空間で、複数のスピーカーから流れる音や声、気配などに意識を向ける。視覚に頼らず、音を身体全体で感じる体験が用意されている。

「参の間」である「質量への憧憬」では、人類が生み出してきた発明品など約170点を展示。カメラや工具をはじめとする様々な道具が鏡の中に並び、無数に広がっていくような光景が目の前に現れる。続く「潜在空間の夢」と題された「肆の間」では、鑑賞者は再びデジタル空間へと戻っていく。最後の「橋」はガラスの向こうに「参の間」が見える部屋で、「記号の彼岸」と題されている。それまで巡ってきた空間を振り返りながら、出口へと向かう。

施設名の「ⁿ」は、結節点を意味する「nexus」に由来。人や体験、場所をつなぐという意味が込められている。

なお、「null²」の世界観を受け継ぐプロジェクトとして、2027年には横浜・上瀬谷で開催される「GREEN×EXPO 2027」に「null⁴（テトラヌル）」も登場予定。4つの鏡面体が回転・振動する彫刻的な作品で、自然の風景を映し込みながら変化する姿を楽しめるという。

editorial_title_zh: 细节中的恶魔：100年过去了，F·W·茂瑙的《浮士德》剪贴簿揭示了其无声电影杰作的秘密
editorial_excerpt_zh: 一本重新被发现的素描和片场照片合集，终于揭示了早期电影最具天赋的先驱之一F·W·茂瑙在片场错综复杂的谜团。他的同辈们……

"F·W·茂瑙是所有无声电影导演中最伟大的导演之一，在银幕上呈现优美影像方面有着罕见的天赋。他的同行们喜欢说他“与其说长着脑袋，不如说长着一台摄影机”。这位曾执导吸血鬼传奇片《诺斯费拉图》（1922）和婚姻浪漫片《日出》（1927）的出色导演于1931年去世，享年42岁，这意味着他的职业生涯几乎刚刚跨入有声片时代。尽管如此，茂瑙高产的无声电影序列中仍然包含了一些优美且常常令人不安的经典之作，他在这些作品中让摄影机在光影交织的变换景致中漫游，并探究了人类灵魂的深处。这一点在他于本月迎来上映100周年的力作《浮士德》中体现得最为淋漓尽致，该片改编自歌德关于与魔鬼交易的戏剧。而《浮士德》的幕后制作则在一本精美的新书中得到了描绘，它既是一份记录，在某种意义上也是这部经典电影制作过程中的一件艺术品。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "茂瑙也是最神秘的导演之一：对自己的方法讳莫如深，对工作投入了极大的热情。早期的合作者埃德加·G·乌尔默（Edgar G Ulmer）称他为“在某种催眠状态下工作的伟大纯粹主义者”。茂瑙禁止制片人进入他的片场，也禁止高管观看他的毛片。除了少数例外，他不允许进行片场摄影以泄露其摄影和特效的秘密。这种神秘感为人们留下了猜测的空间，即茂瑙或是他那才华横溢的工作人员，究竟谁才应对其电影的成功负责。《浮士德圣经：F·W·茂瑙杰作的幕后制作》一书公布了其最佳电影之一拍摄期间未曾公开的影像，并为人们深入了解其合作制作方式提供了难得的视角。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/5fc337135f6fc9e46a53cec1cf295016fe1e740b/0_0_1684_1250/master/1684.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "F·W·茂瑙在《浮士德》片场，由汉斯·纳特格拍摄。", "caption": "由汉斯·纳特格（Hans Natge）拍摄的在《浮士德》片场中的F·W·茂瑙。照片：© 法国电影资料馆，巴黎", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《浮士德》是茂瑙前往好莱坞之前在德国拍摄的最后一部电影，在当时也是乌发电影公司（Ufa）制作过的预算最高、最复杂的电影。它是对歌德悲剧的改编，讲述了学者浮士德（由瑞典演员约斯塔·埃克曼饰演）将灵魂出卖给魔鬼的故事，魔鬼则由咧嘴笑着、身穿黑衣的恶魔墨菲斯托费利斯（德国明星埃米尔·雅宁斯饰演）扮演。《浮士德》在上映时遭遇了商业惨败，如今却被尊为影史巨作。法国新浪潮导演埃里克·侯麦（Éric Rohmer）是茂瑙的狂热追随者，他曾撰写关于该片的博士论文。《浮士德圣经》揭示了茂瑙及其剧组如何在片中实现那些令人难以置信的镜头和特效，但它同时也是该片制作过程中一件文物的增强版复制品，这件文物历经重重磨难得以幸存，从而泄露了它的秘密。在电影中，浮士德拥有一本厚重的皮革装帧圣经，他在绝望时刻将其扔进火中。但这件道具后来变成了更具意义的东西。艺术指导罗伯特·赫尔特（Robert Herlth）和沃尔特·勒里格（Walter Röhrig）将这本书从灰烬中抢救出来，并把设计图、剧照和幕后照片贴在空白书页上，以便在拍摄结束时将这份纪念品作为礼物送给导演。茂瑙去好莱坞时把它留在了柏林的公寓里，当时他并不知道自己再也无法回去取回它。在他去世后，茂瑙的兄弟将他的随身物品藏在市中心各处的地下室里，而在第二次世界大战期间柏林开始遭受轰炸时，这些地下室极易发生水灾以及更糟糕的情况。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://i.guim.co.uk/img/media/f52a21ce08b0f58f4629635791b22230f8ec4f57/152_32_979_783/master/979.jpg?width=445&dpr=1&s=none&crop=none", "alt": "身着墨菲斯托和浮士德戏服的埃米尔·雅宁斯与约斯塔·埃克曼。", "caption": "身着墨菲斯托和浮士德戏服的埃米尔·雅宁斯与约斯塔·埃克曼。照片：© 法国电影资料馆，巴黎", "credit": "The Guardian · Culture", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "电影学者兼档案管理员洛特·艾斯纳（Lotte Eisner）在20世纪50年代来到柏林寻找穆瑙的档案，但没有找到这本圣经的任何踪迹。直到20世纪60年代，该市艺术学院（Akademie der Künste）的一位德国策展人恩格尔贝特·冯·马林克罗特（Engelbert von Mallinckrodt）告诉法国电影资料馆（Cinémathèque Française）的亨利·朗格瓦（Henri Langlois），他从一位与电影界有渊源、名叫罗尔夫·孔辛切（Rolf "翻开内页，各个场景的草图与电影中对应的剧照左右相对。翻阅这些神圣的页面，你可以看到被称为“电影建筑师”的设计师们如何将人物与物体的构图——强迫透视、明暗对比的安排、横扫的阴影、蒸汽与火焰——通过穆瑙和他的才华横溢的摄影师卡尔·霍夫曼（Carl Hoffmann）在电影中重新创造出来。导演鼓励他的设计师不仅要绘制空间，还要绘制演员，从而创造出比布景设计更接近分镜头的图像。", article_text:
F W Murnau was one of the greatest of all silent film-makers, with a rare genius for making beautiful images on screen. His peers liked to say he “had a camera instead of a head”. The director of such stunning films as vampire tale Nosferatu (1922) and marital romance Sunrise: A Song of Two Humans (1927) died at the age of 42 in 1931, meaning that his career barely scraped into the talkie era. Still, Murnau’s tremendous run of silent pictures included some beautiful, often disturbing classics, in which he sent his camera roaming through changing vistas of shadows and light, and plumbed the depths of the human soul. Nowhere more so than in his tour-de-force Faust, released 100 years ago this month, based on Goethe’s play about a deal with the devil. And the making of Faust is depicted in a stunning new book, which is both a document of, and in a sense an artefact from, the production of this classic film.

Murnau was also one of the most mysterious of directors: secretive about his methods, with an intense devotion to his work. Early collaborator Edgar G Ulmer called him “a great purist who worked under a sort of hypnosis”. Murnau banned producers from his sets, and executives from watching his rushes. Bar a few exceptions, he did not allow on-set photography to reveal the secrets of his camerawork and special effects. This mystique created room for speculation as to whether Murnau, or his talented crew, were responsible for the success of his films. The Faust Bible: The Making of FW Murnau’s Masterpiece publishes unseen images from the shoot of one of his best films, and gives a rare insight into the collaborative way it was made.

Faust was Murnau’s final German film before he went to Hollywood, and at the time it was the most expensive, complex film that the Ufa studio had ever produced. It is an adaptation of Goethe’s tragedy about the scholar Faust (played by Swedish actor Gösta Ekman) who sells his soul to the devil, represented by the grinning, black-clad demon Mephistopheles (German star Emil Jannings). A commercial flop on its release, Faust is now acclaimed as one of the greats. French New Wave director Éric Rohmer, a Murnau devotee, wrote his doctoral dissertation on the film. The Faust Bible reveals how Murnau and his crew achieved some of the incredible shots and special effects in this film, but it is also an enhanced facsimile of an artefact from the film’s production, which has survived against all odds to spill its secrets. In the film, Faust owns a hefty, leather-bound Bible, which he throws on the fire in a moment of despair. But the prop was to become something more. Art directors Robert Herlth and Walter Röhrig pulled the book from the ashes and pasted designs, stills and behind-the-scenes photographs on to its blank pages so they could present the souvenir as a gift to the director at the end of the shoot. Murnau left it behind in his flat in Berlin when he went to Hollywood, not knowing he would never return to retrieve it. After his death, Murnau’s brother stashed his belongings in various city-centre basements, which were susceptible to flooding, and worse, once the bombs began falling on Berlin during the second world war.

Film scholar and archivist Lotte Eisner came to Berlin looking for Murnau’s archives in the 1950s, but found no sign of the Bible. It was not until the 1960s that a German curator from the city’s Akademie der Künste, Engelbert von Mallinckrodt, told Henri Langlois at the Cinématheque Française that he had bought some of Murnau’s photo albums for a small sum from a restaurateur called Rolf Conscienze, who had film industry connections. It turned out that these albums included the Bible – though no one knows how they ended up with Conscienze. Then, to deepen the mystery, Mallinckrodt vanished, and his flatmate became the book’s custodian for several decades: it was wrapped in brown paper sitting on top of a cupboard. Eisner searched for the Faust Bible her whole life but she was never to see it. She died in 1983.

Now the book is in the safekeeping of the Cinémathèque Française, which bought it in 2017, and there it remains, a memento of the once-contested collaborative nature of Murnau’s methods. I went to see it this summer, and it is appropriately grand in scale, an unusually majestic scrapbook. Restored by the cinema’s director of heritage Laurent Mannoni and his team, the book looks good for an abandoned, 100-year-old prop. The water-damage has been smoothed out, leaving only a few scuffs, and the shadows where some enterprising thief has prised the metal crucifix and corner pieces from the leather.

Inside, sketches for individual scenes are arranged opposite matching stills from the film. Turning these hallowed pages, you can see how the compositions of figures and objects by the designers known as “film architects” – the forced perspectives, contrasting arrangements of light and dark, sweeping shadows, steam and flames – were re-created on film by Murnau and his talented cinematographer Carl Hoffmann. The director encouraged his designer to draw not just the spaces, but the actors too, creating something closer to a storyboard image than a set design.

“The sketch became the equivalent of a contract,” Herlth later wrote. “[Murnau] insisted that every stroke of the pen should be faithfully rendered in the execution.” This meant not only building sets according to the designs but Murnau and Hoffmann making extensive adjustments to the lighting to produce the velvety shadows that the director demanded. Hoffmann then navigated these settings with bold, fluid camera movements in a technique called entfesselte Kamera (unchained camera), originated by cinematographer Karl Freund when working with Murnau on The Last Laugh (1924). Murnau was not short of visual references. He had a strong interest in the occult, and his background was in art history. Albrecht Dürer’s Four Horsemen of the Apocalypse woodcut was a direct influence on the film’s opening scene.

Herlth recalled the experience of working with Murnau as good-humoured, if challenging, as the director was cheerful but always ambitious to create shots and camera effects that had not been achieved before. The crew spent long days and nights discussing and experimenting with new ideas. “Each day on the set was a fresh opportunity to surpass ourselves in inventiveness and ingenuity,” he said.

Leafing further through the Bible, the chiaroscuro sketches and stills give way to playful collages, images of the cast and crew having fun on set, the legendarily tall Murnau hunched over as he instructs Jannings how to leer malevolently. And there are pages that speak to that boundless technical ingenuity. One of the most celebrated moments in the film is the Weltflug (“flight around the world”) sequence, in which Mephistopheles flies Faust through the sky on his cloak, the world lurching below them. The Bible retains the diagrams that explain just how they achieved this uncanny flight simulation. The secret was a low wooden trolley moving along a plaster ramp, an idea that came to Herlth and Röhrig when they saw a truck being unloaded in the street.

The facsimile edition reprints the Weltflug diagrams on gatefold pages so you can study century-old secrets of film technique at your leisure. It also comprehensively reprints all the Bible’s images, with explanatory captions, enlargements, and quotations from the screenplay, which was written in epigrammatic, almost poetic prose. There are also essays and additional drawings from the Cinémathèque’s archives.

We may never fully understand the workings of Murnau’s mysterious “camera-head” and his collaborations with his team. But this fascinating souvenir takes us close.

The Faust Bible (Mubi Editions, £75). To support the Guardian, order your copy at guardianbookshop.com . Delivery charges may apply.

Faust streams on Mubi from 14 October, with live-scored centenary screenings in Paris on 17 October, Munich on 25 October, and Los Angeles on 1 November

title_original: Gu You on The First Taste of Loneliness and Returning to a “More Honest Way” of Filmmaking
editorial_title_zh: 顾裕谈《初尝孤独》与回归“更真诚的电影创作方式”
editorial_excerpt_zh: 三代女性在导演顾裕的三部曲终章《初尝孤独》中直面悲痛。他的处女作《春江水暖》（2019）曾入围戛纳电影节。随后是2023年的《草木人间》。《初尝孤独》由著名的……
editorial_blocks_json: [{"type": "paragraph", "text": "三代女性在导演顾裕的三部曲终章《初尝孤独》中直面悲痛。他的处女作《春江水暖》（2019）曾入围戛纳电影节。随后是2023年的《草木人间》。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《初尝孤独》由知名中国演员周迅饰演江月，她是一位刚失去设计工作的离异母亲。她回到家中协助母亲露娜（奚美娟饰）照顾病重的丈夫。月月的女儿小满（王圣迪饰）是一名高中生，正努力适应以祖父病情为中心的家庭生活。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "通过与日本摄影师泷本干也合作，顾裕采用了一种部分根植于中国山水画的引人注目的视觉手法。镜头从右向左移动，仿佛徐徐展开一幅画卷，在长达数分钟的镜头中，耐心穿梭于雄伟的风景与私密的内景之间。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "影片的时间感是流动的，过去、现在和未来在同一个画幅中交织。顾裕在iPhone上向我指出，长卷画作如何能够将不同的时间和场景结合在一起。顾裕电影中弥漫着一种失落感，一种生命因死亡的降临而被彻底改变的感觉。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们在2026年釜山国际电影节上采访了这位导演，该片在那里进行了主竞赛单元的首映，并斩获两个奖项：周迅荣获最佳演员奖，李丹枫荣获釜山奖项之艺术贡献奖（特别针对声音设计）。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "《电影舞台》：这是一部非常复杂的电影。拍出来一定很难。尤其是摄影。镜头一直在动。有时，在我看来，它似乎在寻找水，寻找作为核心视觉母题的那条河。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "顾裕：镜头其实是在寻找家庭成员。你提到的那些镜头在水边及河流周围找到了祖代的三位女性。镜头采用的是祖父的视角。当它看到江月在哭泣时，它也在寻找家里的其他人。可以说，这部电影是祖父去世前的最后100天。从某种意义上说，镜头就像他的灵魂。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "能谈谈你的视觉处理手法吗？为什么要使用超长镜头？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "视觉效果是基于情感和哲学的。但我先想谈谈技术。我的三部电影都以中国古代艺术形式山水画为基础。我们为拍摄设定了规则，第一条就是镜头必须始终从右向左移动。这对应着古代画卷徐徐展开的方式。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "第二条规则是将不同的场景和地点融入同一个镜头中——这是一种重现画卷中那种可以看到空间和时间的流动或转换的技巧。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我试图做的是限制我们的拍摄方式，以寻找新的拍片途径。因为现在我们看到人们在用AI创作电影。每个人都能接触到各种各样的电影制作方法。已经不再存在所谓的“不正确”风格。我用我的规则或原则来限制或回归一种更真诚的拍摄方式——不仅对中国电影，对所有文化的电影都是如此。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url": "https://thefilmstage.com/wp-content/uploads/2026/10/Gu-You-801x1200.jpg", "alt": "", "caption": "", "credit": "The Film Stage", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "顾裕", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你有一个关于山神庙的镜头，其中包含了多个时间线。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我是故意模仿山水画的视角的。这些画作与欧洲绘画或照片截然不同。欧洲的一幅画可能会描绘一个角色或一个时间点。山水画则包含许多时间和地点。你可以把画卷的展开想象成剪辑或剪切。在一个地方，你可能会看到全部四个季节。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "山水画中有一种所谓的“鸟瞰视角”，可以飞越时间和空间。这就像乘坐热气球旅行。对于年长的中国人来说，欣赏山水画就像在看一场过去的电影。他们实际上是在展开画卷，因此他们也随之在旅行。我们用作海报的那幅山水画，前景中的那些树实际上来自山顶。画家只是把它们移到了画面的前部。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "这是我拍这部电影的灵感来源，因为我们可以拍摄一定的时间和空间，但如何将它们结合起来取决于观众。例如，在第二个长镜头中，蒙太奇是在向前推进，但故事本身却在倒退。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "还有一个镜头可能会让观众觉得很有挑战性。江月和她的母亲露娜去餐馆见徐先生及其家人。在镜头的开头，我们看到徐先生在洗手间洗手，但在画外音中，我们听到徐先生在餐馆里介绍自己的家人。随着镜头的延续，我们听到徐先生在桌旁说他要去男厕所。我们本可以按线性顺序剪辑，但我希望尝试把整个场景结合在一个空间里，而不管时间如何。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我很想知道你是如何设计镜头的。露娜的公寓里有一个长长的移动镜头，聚焦在几个细节上：照片、雕塑、牌匾。这个镜头是写出来的还是有分镜头脚本，亦或是更多地与摄影师合作完成的？", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "比较困难的镜头的细节我们会画出来或做成故事板，以便向摄影指导解释我们的需求。但这也是一个更长的过程。我们在开拍前把那套公寓租了几个月。这样我们就可以根据需要进行尽可能长时间的筹备和排练。可以说，大部分镜头都是由我设计然后由摄影指导执行的。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "但以公园里的夜景为例，Luna在那儿和徐先生跳舞。当徐先生出镜后，她独自继续跳舞。摄像机环绕着她旋转，在华尔兹音乐勾起她眼泪的瞬间推进到特写。现场有灯光需要处理，她身后还有许多群众演员。摄像机依然得想办法捕捉到Luna的情绪。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "你刚才说这部电影拍起来很难，你说得对。不仅是因为那些漫长无比的长镜头，还因为我合作的演员在中国都非常有名。我们把他们带到公众场所，旁观者看到他们会非常兴奋。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "我们必须在没人的时候排练，比如半夜。我们一遍遍走他们要走的路线、他们将如何行走、我们又该如何拍摄。一旦到了实拍时，你只有一个镜头，只有一次机会。", "translated": true}, {"type": "paragraph", "text": "在拍摄Luna的那个镜头时，我们用隐藏摄像机从不同角度进行捕捉，并在她身后安排了演员，以便我们能对上镜头。但如果我们第一条没能拍到想要的，就得换地方，因为所有围观群众都会看出我们在拍电影。", "translated": true}, {"type": "image", "url":
